title: eunox effect contract (registry corpus entry)
description: One entry in the eunox effect-contract registry: an effect contract plus the identity, provenance, and content digest a shared corpus needs. The registry is authoring-time input, never a runtime dependency — eunox does not fetch a contract while deciding. A manifest carries the contract inline and optionally pins the entry it was authored from via `effect.ref` ("<id>@<digest>"), which the manifest loader verifies locally by recomputing the digest. Trust model is package signing, not behavioral verification: a contract asserts what a tool does, and nothing here observes whether that is true.

schemaVersion.description: Corpus entry grammar version. Independent of the manifest schemaVersion: an entry is a distributed artifact with its own compatibility story.

id.description: Corpus-unique contract identifier, "<publisher>/<server>.<tool>". It is the half of a manifest `effect.ref` before the '@'.

tool.description: The advertised MCP tool name this contract describes.

server.description: The MCP server that advertises the tool.

name.description: Package or service identifier as its publisher spells it.

homepage.description: Where a reviewer goes to check the claim.

versionRange.description: Server versions whose advertised surface matches what was reviewed. Absent means the contract is believed stable across versions — which is itself a claim, so record it deliberately.

summary.description: One-line description of what the tool does. Prose for a human reviewer; never parsed, never an input to a decision.

notes.description: The reasoning behind the class, especially where the obvious reading is wrong (why an apparently undoable action is irreversible; why a compensable one is not therefore safe). This is the part a reviewer reviews.

attestation.description: Provenance and review state — the trust surface, deliberately modest: authorship and review, not a verification claim.

source.description: authored = written by hand from the tool's documented behavior; vendor = contributed by the server's publisher; imported = derived from an orchestrator's existing compensation definitions (has-compensation implies compensable, neither-compensated-nor-idempotent implies irreversible).

review.description: Review state. NOT a correctness guarantee.

signatures.description: Signed statements about this entry: a vendor attesting that the contract describes their tool, a reviewer who read it, or either DISPUTING it. Verified LOCALLY against a trusted-key file the operator supplies (`eunox contracts --trust-keys`) — never fetched, and never on the decision path. Deliberately OUTSIDE the digest: each signature is over the digest, so including them would be circular and every added countersignature would invalidate every manifest pin to the entry.

keyId.description: Names the key that produced the signature, matched against the operator's trusted-key file. A signature whose key is absent from that file is reported as unverified, never as an error — a corpus may be signed by parties you have not chosen to trust.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. One value, chosen rather than negotiated: an algorithm field a verifier honors is an algorithm an attacker selects.

role.description: Standing the signer claims: vendor = the party publishing the MCP server; reviewer = a third party who read the entry. Part of the SIGNED payload, so a reviewer's signature cannot be re-presented as a vendor's.

statement.description: attests = the contract correctly describes the tool; disputes = it does not. Part of the SIGNED payload, so a dispute cannot be edited into an endorsement. A dispute is a community-advisory signal, never a scanner verdict.

signature.description:
Base64 (standard encoding) Ed25519 signature over the newline-joined payload "eunox-effect-contract-attestation/v1
<id>
<digest>
<role>
<statement>". `eunox contracts --attest-payload <id>` prints those exact bytes.

digest.description: sha256 of the `effect` block's canonical JSON encoding — the value a manifest pins after the '@'. Two entries with identical contract content share a digest; identity lives in `id`, integrity in `digest`.

effectClass.description: The closed reversibility vocabulary, ordered least to most consequential. Flat and totally ordered on purpose: no lattice until a partner forces a partial order.

blastRadius.description: How much one call affects. Exactly one of `value` or `argument`. Absent entirely means unquantified, which exceeds any finite bound — an action whose size cannot be established must not be treated as small.

value.description: A fixed magnitude for every call to this target.

argument.description: The call argument carrying the magnitude. A list argument contributes its LENGTH; a non-numeric string has no magnitude and resolves to unquantified rather than being counted by characters.

unit.description: Free-form label for reports and audit records ("usd", "rows", "recipients"). Never compared — eunox models no unit algebra — so two contracts on one target must agree by convention, not by check.

effectCase.description: One row of an argument-parameterized contract. A row is a contract, and obeys the same rules.

effectContract.description: What a call DOES, as PDP-addressable policy input — replacing a server's self-declared, unauthenticated hints. Note the absence of a `ref` here: a corpus entry IS the thing a ref points at, and a self-reference is excluded from the digest.

idempotent.description: The call can be safely repeated with no additional effect. It does not by itself make an action reversible — a repeatable outbound email is still irreversible — but it is what lets a retry count as one action.

compensatingAction.description: The target that reverses this one. Required for class `compensable` and rejected on any other: "compensable with nothing to compensate with" is irreversible wearing a softer label, and the consequence gate must not accept that mislabel.

byArgument.description: The argument-parameterized form: effect as a function of one argument, expressed as a STATIC decision table (db.query reversible for SELECT, irreversible for DROP). Resolved from the call's own arguments on the decision path — no callout, no inference. A table, not an expression, because a table is reviewable and pinnable and an expression must be executed to be understood.

cases.description: Argument value to contract overlay. For an operation-style argument the first whitespace-delimited token is matched too, so "DROP" matches "DROP TABLE users" — the same coarse first-verb rule allowedOperations uses, with the same limit that it is not a SQL parser.

default.description: Applies when the call supplies a value the cases do not cover. ABSENT means the fail-closed default (irreversible, unquantified), not the base contract: a table that does not cover a value has not said the value is safe. A call that establishes no value at all — the argument omitted, an unresolvable path, null, blank, or a composite no case key can name — resolves fail-closed whether or not a default is declared.

allOf.description: A compensating action is what makes an action compensable, so it may not appear with any other class.
